notify.title.message: Requests come through a proxy ReputeCast doesn't trust
notify.title.note: notification title for instance admins; a proxy is the reverse proxy or load balancer in front of ReputeCast

notify.body.message: {peer} forwards requests to ReputeCast with {header}, but {setting} doesn't list it. Every open and click looks like it comes from {peer}, so the bot filter can't see readers' addresses. Add {peer} to {setting} (environment variable {env}) and restart ReputeCast.
notify.body.note: {setting} and {env} are configuration names, never translated; {header} is an HTTP header name

advice.none: No request came through a proxy ReputeCast doesn't trust.

advice.some.message: Add these addresses to {setting} (environment variable {env}) and restart ReputeCast, so opens, clicks and rate limits see readers' own addresses.
advice.some.note: {setting} and {env} are configuration names, never translated

notify.publicTitle.message: Most requests carry forwarding headers from a public address
notify.publicTitle.note: notification title for instance admins; a public address is one on the internet, not on the instance's own network

notify.publicBody.message: Requests from {peer} carry forwarding headers ({header}), and for a while most of ReputeCast's traffic has come that way. If {peer} belongs to your CDN or load balancer, add the address ranges it sends from, as its provider publishes them, to {setting} (environment variable {env}) and restart ReputeCast. If you don't recognize {peer}, change nothing: anyone can send these headers, and an address ReputeCast trusts can make up readers' addresses.
notify.publicBody.note: {setting} and {env} are configuration names, never translated; {header} is an HTTP header name. Never tell admins to add {peer} itself: anyone can send forwarding headers

advice.public.message: Add the addresses from your own network to {setting} (environment variable {env}) and restart ReputeCast. Don't add a public address as it is: if it belongs to your CDN or load balancer, add the address ranges it sends from, as its provider publishes them; if you don't recognize it, leave it out, since anyone can send forwarding headers.
advice.public.note: {setting} and {env} are configuration names, never translated; shown when one of the listed addresses is public
